name: Pedro the Lion
label: Jade Tree
lede: A pastor's son wrote Jade Tree's darkest records almost entirely by himself, split his Christian audience with a record about adultery and murder, shut the band down in 2006, and then revived it to tell the story of his own childhood.

eras.title: Pastor's son, Seattle drummer
eras.text: David Bazan grew up a pastor's son and came up in 1990s Seattle, where Tooth & Nail sold Christian punk and Built to Spill was rewriting guitar rock. He started Pedro the Lion in 1995 and ended up writing almost all of it himself.

years.h: David Bazan is born in Phoenix, Arizona
years.p: His Arizona childhood becomes the subject of Pedro the Lion's comeback album, Phoenix, 43 years later.

years.src: Wikipedia: David Bazan · Wikipedia: Pedro the Lion · Stereogum
years.h: Bazan drums for a high school friend, then starts his own band
years.p: At Shorewood High School in Washington he met [[Damien Jurado|f4805b9d-68f8-438e-8f13-ec7bcb4c8581]], and played drums in Jurado's band the Guilty, later Coolidge. In 1995 he started Pedro the Lion in Seattle.

years.h: Seasick Steve records Pedro's first EP
years.p: Steven Gene Wold, years before he was famous, was Bazan's spiritual mentor. He played occasional slide guitar and recorded Whole for Tooth & Nail.

eras.title: A label built for one band
eras.text: A Tooth & Nail publicist started Made in Mexico just to release Pedro's first album, and Jade Tree took the next records. Bazan played nearly everything himself and started writing concept albums about sin and power.

years.src: Wikipedia: It's Hard to Find a Friend
years.h: Big Trucks: 1,000 copies, and a label with one band
years.p: Tooth & Nail publicist James Morelos started Made in Mexico for Bazan alone, and this single was its first release.

years.src: Wikipedia: It's Hard to Find a Friend · Stereogum
yt: Live at the Coffee Shock, St. Paul, 1998
years.h: Bazan tapes It's Hard to Find a Friend to reel-to-reel
years.p: Bazan sang and played guitar and drums, with Johnathon Ford on bass. Pitchfork's Jeremy Schneyer gave it 7.8 and compared it to Luna.
years.xp:
Made in Mexico existed to put this album out. KEXP's Dusty Henry later called it the lushest-sounding recording in Bazan's catalog.

Jade Tree reissued a remaster on October 16, 2001, which is how most fans found it. The video is a full 1998 set from the Coffee Shock in St. Paul.

years.h: The Only Reason I Feel Secure goes out on two labels
years.p: Made in Mexico and Jade Tree share the release of Pedro's second EP.

years.h: Sub Pop's singles club gets a Pedro record
years.p: Song A / Song B is pressed in 1,300 copies for Sub Pop's subscription series.

years.h: A corrupt politician rises and falls on Winners Never Quit
years.p: Pedro's first concept album, Jade Tree JT1046, has Bazan on every instrument. Pitchfork gave it a 4.1, and Bazan called the review ad hominem.
years.xp:
Bazan summed up the story as "Damnation for the arrogant, judgment for the judgmental." It aimed at hypocrisy in the church as much as in politics.

Metacritic averaged it at 72. Salon praised Bazan for conveying "the horror and contorted anguish of his protagonist without trivializing either." AllMusic called it mostly "a curiosity." Bazan answered the faith-based criticism on his 2006 album Fewer Moving Parts.

A Japanese bonus track is an alternate take of the opener featuring [[Ben Gibbard|02031e5c-f9ab-4b4e-bc08-a61ea11a455d]].

years.h: Ben Gibbard takes a turn on bass
years.p: The [[Death Cab for Cutie|0039c7ae-e1a7-4a7d-9b49-0cbc716821a6]] singer plays bass for a stretch in 2000. Two future [[Fleet Foxes|fa97dd36-1b82-43d7-a6e4-2adeafd59cef]] members also pass through before that band exists.

years.h: A single and a storybook
years.p: Suicide Squeeze presses 2,000 copies of Progress / A Guitar for Janie, packaged with a storybook.

eras.title: Control, and the listeners who objected
eras.text: Control was Pedro's heaviest record and its bleakest story, a cheating businessman killed by his wife. Some of Bazan's Christian audience turned on him, and by Achilles Heel TW Walsh was co-writing alongside him.

years.cap: Pedro the Lion on an outdoor festival stage, July 2002
years.h: Pedro the Lion's heaviest record is about an affair and a murder
years.p: A businessman cheats and his wife kills him, set against the 1999 WTO protests that inspired it. [[Casey Foubert|739b77af-80b8-4896-ac4c-e8a922c9390a]] plays bass, and it reaches No. 36 on the independent chart.
years.xp:
Stereogum called it "the heaviest Pedro the Lion album, both in tone and sonically": distorted guitars, prominent drums, synths. Foubert also co-wrote Penetration and Second Best.

Bazan said it wasn't autobiographical, only his "disappointment with the world and how it works." Metacritic averaged it at 75, Pitchfork gave it a 7.2, and some Christian listeners took the dark story as an attack.

q: I don't know if I would have made Control if I wasn't on that label.
years.h: Jade Tree likes the fast songs, so Bazan goes heavy
years.p: Bazan recalls the comments from his label after It's Hard to Find a Friend. He says he didn't understand what Jade Tree wanted from the band.
years.xp:
Bazan told Stereogum the label pressure "probably influenced me to make more sort of like heavy records."

Not everyone followed him there. On the Control tour, some Christian fans objected to the darker, more cynical songs, and Wikipedia describes the fanbase as divided by the record.

years.h: Bazan appears in a documentary about Christian rock
years.p: Why Should the Devil Have All the Good Music? (2004) features Pedro the Lion.

years.cap: David Bazan playing solo acoustic as Pedro the Lion
years.h: TW Walsh joins, and Pitchfork gives Achilles Heel a 4.7
years.p: [[TW Walsh|80eb65f4-5a8f-4aaa-8bcd-4961b55f5971]] co-wrote Keep Swinging and wrote Start Without Me. AllMusic gave the record 4.5 out of 5.
years.xp:
Bazan called it less bleak and more multi-faceted than Control. It reached No. 26 on Heatseekers and No. 24 on the independent chart, and Metacritic averaged it at 71.

Pitchfork called it "topographically uniform" and a "stumble." AllMusic heard "a beautiful and wavering mix of indie rock and country-folk." The A.V. Club found "exquisitely wrought, inimitably pessimistic epiphanies" in a record it also called a hodge-podge.

years.h: Headphones starts up on the side
years.p: Bazan begins the project a year before he retires the Pedro the Lion name.

eras.title: The brand name of his dysfunction
eras.text: Bazan ended Pedro the Lion in early 2006 and went out under his own name. His solo debut, Curse Your Branches, laid out his break with Christianity, and for years he made more money playing alone than he ever had as Pedro.

q: At the time, Pedro The Lion was the brand name of my dysfunction.
years.src: Stereogum: Control · Wikipedia: Pedro the Lion
years.h: Bazan retires the Pedro the Lion name, and nobody storms out
years.p: The split is announced in early January 2006 and is amicable. [[TW Walsh|80eb65f4-5a8f-4aaa-8bcd-4961b55f5971]] goes back to web development and his band The Soft Drugs.
years.xp:
Bazan called himself "a prickly collaborator" and said he felt guilty about driving people away. He had written 90 to 100 percent of the material, Walsh was his only real cowriter, and the strain led Walsh to leave.

They made up. Bazan's statement said their friendship had "even been strengthened by the breakup."

years.src: Wikipedia: David Bazan · Wikipedia: Pedro the Lion
years.h: Bazan's first solo album is about losing his faith
years.p: Curse Your Branches debuts at No. 1 on Heatseekers and No. 116 on the Billboard 200. Bazan plays every instrument.
years.xp: The Barsuk record was previewed on his fall 2008 tour, where he played Weeds in the Wheat, Broken Arm and In Stitches before anyone could buy it.

yt: Bazan plays Pedro the Lion songs, KEXP, December 2012
years.h: TW Walsh remasters the old Pedro records for vinyl
years.p: Walsh, back on good terms with Bazan, handles the reissues. That December Bazan plays Pedro songs solo at KEXP.

years.h: Bazan signs on with Overseas
years.p: The band is [[Will Johnson|9e455882-2bb2-47fa-b1ce-f8516123649d]] of Centro-matic and Bubba and Matt Kadane of Bedhead and [[The New Year|b3d5b1c9-95df-42ea-83eb-c86b18f61f8d]].

eras.title: Home to the old name
eras.text: Tired of touring alone, Bazan put a band back together and gave it the old name. The comeback became a planned five-album autobiography that starts with his Phoenix childhood.

years.h: After eleven years solo, Bazan brings the band back
years.p: He announces the return on October 4 with Erik Walters and Terence Ankeny. The first shows follow that December.
years.xp:
Bazan said he missed the energy of making music with other people, and that he "needed to be in a band again." He first thought of billing it as the David Bazan Band.

By mid-summer he realized he'd fallen back into the process that made the first three Pedro records. "To my surprise, it felt a bit like coming home."

He also told Stereogum he made three times as much playing shows as Pedro than under his own name.

years.h: Phoenix opens a five-album autobiography
years.p: The first Pedro record in 15 years, on Polyvinyl, covers Bazan's Arizona childhood: bikes, model homes, desert. It goes to No. 1 on Heatseekers.
years.xp:
Andy D. Park produced the 13 songs, which run 45 minutes. Havasu and Santa Cruz continue the cycle.

Metacritic averaged it at 79 and it reached No. 10 on the independent chart. The 405 said Bazan "returns to Pedro The Lion in order to rediscover himself."

years.h: A documentary follows Bazan through the 2016 election
years.p: Brandon Vedder's Strange Negotiations tracks Bazan's spiritual and personal turmoil. Bazan supplies the music.

years.h: Havasu arrives without warning
years.p: Part two of the autobiography cycle goes up on Polyvinyl with no advance notice.

years.h: Chapter three is Santa Cruz
years.p: Polyvinyl releases the third installment. That September Pedro covers B by [[Lync|65e1b41c-c719-4237-9f72-c2f07ea19355]] for a Suicide Squeeze split.

years.h: Pedro the Lion goes out with Grandaddy
years.p: Stereogum announces the band as support on [[Grandaddy|9d4c4835-c71a-4647-a4fc-263e26832cd0]]'s 25th anniversary tour for The Sophtware Slump.
